paragraphs: The CLK 320 has been part of the CLK range since 1997, and across its two generations has used two different V6 petrol engines. First-generation cars (C208, 1997-2003) use the M112 - a 3.2-litre V6 that was widely used across Mercedes models of that era. Second-generation cars (C209, 2002-2009) switched to the M272, a more modern V6 with a different architecture. Knowing which one your car has matters, because the components and rebuild specifics differ between them - which is exactly why we confirm your exact engine by registration before quoting.
about.boldParagraph: We continue to rebuild and replace M256 engines for every CLK 320 on the road.

compatibility.intro: Because the CLK 320 spans two distinct V6 engines across two generations, fitting the wrong replacement - or assuming an M112 part will work on an M272 car - risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (M256) via registration or VIN
Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic CLK quote - it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
